core.title: Gather baseline measurements before claiming an alternative is faster
core.given: A plan artifact considers a non-reference execution strategy for a journey.
core.when: You claim that strategy is faster.
core.then: Gather baseline measurements before you claim another strategy is faster.
avoid: Claiming another strategy is faster without baseline measurements.
core.why: Reference execution is the default, not a mandated slow path; it stays the choice when performance evidence does not justify an alternative.
evidence: Baseline measurements were gathered before the speed claim was made.
verification: Advisory boundary: this is guidance for agents, not independent enforcement; existing plan and source validators still apply, and a finding does not introduce new runtime dispatch behavior.
Severity 3, disposition advisory: a finding surfaces as advice and does not fail the run.
Detecting the speed claim needs a new observer over plan artifacts and diffs; until the stack provides one, the change fact is judged by an LLM.

values: claim that a non-reference journey strategy is faster

fires: A plan or doc proposes a non-reference strategy for a journey and says it is faster.
A planner argues for leaving reference execution on performance grounds.
doesNotFire: The plan keeps reference execution and makes no speed claim.
A performance claim with no journey, route or continuation context.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete planner-facing artifact kinds in which a journey strategy or speed claim may be stated; the rule's activation scans these kinds.
The concrete acceptance-side artifact kinds in which a strategy claim may also be stated.

bunOnly.reason: It references the ATDD-Bun sidecar's shared-context block by id, a realization mechanism with no stack-neutral equivalent; the generic meaning of that block (advisory boundary, not independent enforcement) is carried in core:verification.

classification.note: Domain-level given; 'journey' and 'non-reference execution strategy' are product-domain terms, not stack terms. 'A plan' restated with the role name 'plan artifact'.
The single obligation; already stack-neutral, kept verbatim.
Already stack-neutral; kept verbatim. Bun has no prefer or unless items, so the core adds none.
'Reference' expanded to 'Reference execution' (the domain's default journey execution semantics, a product concept, not a stack mechanism); otherwise verbatim.

The shared-context id is ATDD-Bun sidecar machinery (bunOnly); its generic content — advisory boundary, guidance not independent enforcement, existing validators still apply — becomes a core:verification entry.
Per convention, per-rule severity and disposition map to core:verification, not to a profile key.

The task terms (journey, interlocking route, train continuation, execution strategy) are product-domain vocabulary, already stack-neutral; kept in the core activation. The Bun note (speed claim required alongside) is preserved by the change fact conjunction and doesNotFire[1].

Role-level kinds in the core; the concrete ATDD-Bun artifact kinds enter through the profile: planner-facing kinds 'plan, wagon, wmbt, journey' (per the Bun note 'planner artifacts where a strategy claim may be made') as plan_artifact kinds, 'acceptance' as acceptance_test kinds.
The change value is domain-level and kept verbatim; 'needs_new_observer' carries the observer gap, and the Bun note's interim LLM judgement is stated in core:verification.

neutralityNotes: The convention is domain-level planning guidance and needed almost no neutralization. 'Journey', 'interlocking route', 'train continuation', 'execution strategy' and 'reference execution' are product-domain terms, kept in the core deliberately; they bind to no profile key because any stack implementing this product shares them. The only stack-specific content was the artifact-kind list (plan, wagon, wmbt, acceptance, journey), which now enters through roles.plan_artifact.kinds / roles.acceptance_test.kinds, and the shared-context verifier reference (bunOnly). 'Severity 3' uses the stack-wide ATDD severity scale and is kept in core:verification per the not-profile-keys convention. The per-fact 'note' strings of bun.json are not part of the core fact schema; their content is preserved via the change-fact conjunction, doesNotFire, profileRequirement meanings and the verification entry about the missing observer over plan artifacts and diffs.
